story.what_it_does: Mazagon Dock is a government-owned builder of warships and submarines. Almost all its revenue comes from the Ministry of Defence (₹11,07,722 lakh of ₹12,83,964 lakh in FY2026), and it says it has zero debt.
story.plans: The annual report says it plans to enhance South Yard waterfront handling capacity, develop a new 12,000 T floating dry dock, and use green tariff energy to reach a 50% renewable target. It also reports 47 indigenised items and a 51% stake acquired in Colombo Shipyard PLC during the year.
story.moat: Being a government-owned builder of warships and submarines, with the Ministry of Defence as its dominant customer, gives it a captive position in this work. The notes do not describe competitors or any other protective advantages, so the strength of this position cannot be judged from them.

scenarios.story: Revenue grew to ₹12,839.64 crore from ₹11,431.88 crore and profit reached ₹2,435.77 crore, with a 16.42% operating margin and 30.40% return on net worth. Deliveries of frigates and submarines, keel-laying events and the planned yard and dry dock expansion could support future work.
signals_to_watch: Whether the total order book stops shrinking from ₹20,535 crore (March 2026)
Progress on the South Yard waterfront and 12,000 T floating dry dock plans

scenarios.story: The company keeps delivering ships and earning steady profits while working through its existing orders. The order book has fallen from ₹23,758 crore to ₹16,443 crore over the period, so results depend on how fast new work arrives.
